edition.alertText: US strikes IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island — confirmed by US military official (Reuters); IRGC launches drones at US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain — 3rd attack in 5 days — Bahrain intercepts, invokes Article 51; tanker struck twice near Khasab — 24 crew evacuated by Oman, 1 Indian sailor missing, 2 injured (Khaleej Times); UKMTO: separate tanker struck by projectile on outbound Hormuz transit — engine-room fire, crew safe; IRGC claims tanker 'heavily damaged' after mine strike; CNN: US intelligence indicates Iran developing plans for dirty bomb in Washington — 7 officials cited — Iran denies, calls claims 'baseless'; Trump warns Iran of 'major price'; Vance: Iran conflict will not become a 'forever war'; Araghchi meets Oman FM Albusaidi in Muscat — talks on restoring Hormuz shipping described as 'constructive'; Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen summit tomorrow (Nov 19) — Iran on agenda; oil rebounds modestly — Brent $92.67 (+0.93%), WTI $85.87 (+0.98%); gold recovers to ~$3,904 from one-year low; Houthis launch drones toward Saudi East-West pipeline; Saudi coalition intercepts drone heading toward Riyadh; USS Theodore Roosevelt and USS George Washington sail together in Arabian Sea; Iraq resumes crude pumping for export via Turkey pipeline; EASA extends Middle East airspace advisory until 2027; Etihad cancels Riyadh/Dammam flights to Nov 30; Khor Mor gas field drone overflight triggers sirens — no strike; North Macedonia foils Iran-linked attack plot in Greece; IMO: 136 maritime security incidents since Mar 1 including 35 in October

situation: The escalation cycle intensified on Tuesday even as the diplomatic calendar tightened ahead of the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen on November 19 — now one day away. US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island, confirmed by a US military official to Reuters, though local officials reported no residential or infrastructure damage. Hours earlier, the IRGC launched another drone attack on the US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain — the third strike in five days — which Bahrain intercepted and destroyed; CENTCOM said no US equipment was damaged and called the IRGC's radar-destruction claim false. Bahrain condemned the 'systematic hostile approach,' invoked Article 51 of the UN Charter, and urged the Security Council to act, while the UAE issued a separate condemnation. The dirty bomb intelligence dominated diplomatic exchanges: CNN reported on November 16 that US intelligence indicates Iran may be developing plans to detonate a dirty bomb in Washington, citing seven US officials who said the plotting reflected options rather than an imminent threat. Iran denied the allegations — FM spokesman Baghaei called them 'baseless,' Araghchi called them 'rubbish' and blamed Israel — while the White House said there were 'no credible threats.' Trump warned Iran would 'pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before' if Washington were targeted, while Vance pledged the Iran conflict would not become a 'forever war.' Araghchi met Oman's FM Albusaidi in Muscat for talks on restoring Hormuz shipping, which Albusaidi described as 'constructive' — the two sides reviewed progress toward political, technical, and practical understandings for unobstructed vessel transit. Qatar urged restraint from all parties, warning that escalation threatens ongoing negotiations.

Oil prices recovered modestly on Tuesday after Monday's 4% crash, with Brent reclaiming $92.67/bbl (+0.93%) and WTI edging up to $85.87/bbl (+0.98%), supported by fresh tanker attacks that reminded markets the attack risk persists even as the supply surplus narrative dominates. The IEA's projection of a Q4 surplus and recovering Middle East exports continued to weigh on sentiment, with Brent still down approximately 20% from its October peak. VLCC supertanker rates continued their decline — the standard VLCC round-trip time charter equivalent fell to $307,160/day, down 66.3% from $912,660/day at the Week 41 peak (Gulf News / Baltic Exchange), with TD34 at WS310.71. Gold recovered from its one-year low to approximately $3,904/oz (+1.17%), a modest bounce after falling to $3,859 on Monday, though the broader trend remains under pressure from expectations of a December Fed rate hike with CME FedWatch odds near 85%. Coal held steady at $145.25/tonne, down from a 24-month high of $152.45 on October 30 but supported by Middle East tensions and high LNG prices. The USS Theodore Roosevelt and USS George Washington sailed together in the Arabian Sea, maintaining three carrier strike groups plus approximately 19 warships in theater — the largest US naval presence since the Iraq war. Iraq's oil minister announced the resumption of crude pumping for export via the pipeline to Turkey's Ceyhan port, a modest positive for supply diversification away from Hormuz.

Shipping attacks continued on Tuesday. The Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas — the same vessel disabled near Khasab on November 16 — was struck a second time on November 17, causing another engine-room fire. The 25-member crew abandoned ship; Oman's Maritime Security Centre evacuated 24 crew, while India's shipping minister reported 21 Indians evacuated, 2 injured, and 1 Indian sailor missing. In a separate incident, UKMTO reported a tanker struck by an unidentified projectile on outbound transit through Hormuz, causing an engine-room fire with all crew safe. The IRGC claimed another tanker was 'heavily damaged' after hitting a mine, though the claims could not be independently verified. The IMO's cumulative count now stands at 136 maritime security incidents since March 1, including 35 in October alone. A drone overflight triggered sirens at Iraq's Khor Mor gas field — still recovering from the November 9 drone strike that halted production and cut 2.8 gigawatts of Kurdistan electricity — but no strike was confirmed. In Yemen, Houthis launched drones toward the Saudi East-West pipeline while Saudi coalition air defenses intercepted a drone heading toward Riyadh. EASA extended its Middle East airspace advisory until 2027, and Etihad cancelled flights between Abu Dhabi and Dammam/Riyadh until November 30, joining flydubai's extended cancellations to November 27. North Macedonia reportedly foiled an Iran-linked attack plot targeting Greece, adding to the extraterritorial threat dimension as IRGC chief Vahidi warned of 'devastating and painful strikes' against any new US or Israeli action.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva at COP31 (Nov 14) warns 45 million people could face severe food insecurity — urges US and Iran to immediately allow ~5 fertilizer vessels/day through Hormuz within 7-10 days. Fertilizer prices up ~30% since blockades began (UN). Sudan food prices doubled in 6 months; Nepal farmers cannot afford fertiliser. Countries facing significant impact: Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka. Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85), down from 4-year high above €101/MWh prior week; EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). LNG crossings at Hormuz reached 32 in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year. IMF projects 2026 GDP contractions: Kuwait and Iraq ~16%, Qatar ~15%.
